Together the context changes uprightness from an instantly obvious choice into judgment that pauses, distinguishes, and reckons.

The HFT's q-w-m coin branch is excluded because its supplied facet is restricted to specified currencies of exact weight, not general calibration; the 17:12 connection note also records a broad rather than specific relation.

findings.claim: The focus's sound work and great recompense can also be read within a contrast of horizons: desire for the immediate is set beside desire for the Hereafter, whose striving is joined to belief and whose degrees are greater, while provision in the present reaches both groups.
findings.mechanism: The focus's deliberate work and reward meet 17:18's immediate desire and accelerated allotment, 17:19's desire and striving for the Hereafter with belief, 17:20's present provision to both groups, and 17:21's greater degrees. This sequence makes the focus's work legible as effort fitted to a desired horizon and lets great recompense open onto a graded scale beyond immediate allotment.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees effort, belief, and reward in relation to what a person seeks over time, while present provision remains common to the contrasted groups.
findings.containment: The focus's sound deeds remain broader than specifically Hereafter-seeking effort, and 17:20 keeps worldly provision in view for both groups. The horizon-matched reading is a contextual compression, not an exclusive definition of every good deed.

epistemic.reason: The HFT coordinates match 17:18, 19, and 21, and the packet separately supplies 17:20's exact text for the shared-provision relation. The compression of the focus phrase into horizon-matched effort remains an inference.

findings.title: A reparative echo in recompense
findings.claim: The promised recompense remains a beneficial return for sound work, and the pericope can also let it carry an exploratory image of repair answering a damaged order.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun أَجْرًا is mapped in the supplied branch registry both to beneficial recompense and, with qualified identity, to joining a broken member. The focus's sound works meet 17:4's corruption, 17:6's return, and 17:16's destruction; these independent contacts make the repair image answer damage at the scale of the order, with crooked or incomplete mending retained as part of the branch's qualified range.
findings.reader_payoff: Reward can be perceived not only as what returns for good work but, tentatively, as a response that helps mend what corruption has damaged.
findings.containment: This is exploratory and analogical: the ordinary recompense reading stays intact, and no literal healing or guaranteed social restoration is asserted. The supplied connection note treats 17:6 chiefly as historical reversal rather than a specific focus claim, so its restoration role remains qualified.

epistemic.reason: The packet maps the qualified repair branch to the exact focus noun, and all cited context roots and indices match. The cross-domain analogy from bone repair to a damaged social order remains multi-step and the HFT source is legacy_unbound.

findings.title: A kinetic echo of uprightness
findings.claim: The focus's most upright direction can carry a qualified bodily-standing echo when the pericope closes this unit with the consequence of sitting blamed and forsaken after divided allegiance.
findings.mechanism: The supplied q-w-m branch F001 places bodily standing on the focus carrier أَقْوَمُ; 17:22 supplies sitting at 17:22:7 and an attributed forsakenness role at 17:22:9. Their contact gives the focus destination a kinetic dimension: upright guidance can sustain action, while the closing consequence pictures its opposite as sitting and abandonment.
findings.reader_payoff: Uprightness becomes perceptible as a posture with consequences in the passage, not only as a static moral label.
findings.containment: The contrast is a reader-constructed echo, not an explicit grammatical antithesis or a lexical claim that أَقْوَمُ means physical standing. The HFT role about weakened legs remains attributed and does not establish the context word's independent branch meaning.

epistemic.reason: The focus and 17:22 carrier coordinates match supplied morphology and context roots. The kinetic antithesis is explicitly reader-constructed, and the context-side legs role has no independent registry descriptor.

findings.title: The guided path becomes a request
findings.claim: As an external overlay, the focus's Quran guiding toward what is most upright meets Fātiḥa's direct request, “Guide us to the straight path”; the reciter thus appears both among those guided by the Quran and among those asking for guidance, while 1:7 gives the path a boundary through favor, anger, and straying.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier يَهْدِى and أَقْوَمُ contacts the external imperative اهْدِنَا and the straight-path phrase in 1:6, with 1:7 continuing that same path through its contrasted descriptions. The relation changes a declarative account of Quranic guidance into a reader-involving loop of receiving and requesting direction.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader is placed inside the guidance relation: the Quran leads, and the reciter asks to be led along the path just named.
findings.containment: This overlay uses only the individually supplied 1:6-7 members; it does not imply a whole-Fātiḥa interpretation or make 1:7 a lexical definition of أَقْوَمُ. Shared roots anchor the contact, while the change from declaration to supplication supplies the additional relation.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and external surfaces show the guide/path contact, while the reciprocal reader position is an interpretive effect of their different speech acts.
